Macrons

Consonantal i

Clothes & getting dressed

underpants noun

also briefs, boxers, boxer shorts, pants

classical

Cic. Off. 1.129
M-O s.v. undershorts

subligāculum, subligāculī n.

noun, second declension

underpants, briefs

Cicero’s word for the loin-cloth that no actor went on stage without; Morgan–Owens gives it, with subligar, for briefs.

Examples

  • Subligāculum indue.

    Put your underpants on.composed

Other words

  • subligar, subligāris n.

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Mart. 3.87.4; Juv. 6.70 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. undershorts

  • femorālia, femorālium n. pl. — coverings for the thighs; boxer shorts

    noun, third declension, plural · also used · late Latin · Vulg. Sir. 45.10 (Lewis & Short, s.v. femorāle); Mir, morning routine; M-O s.v. undershorts

    Mir’s word for underpants; Morgan–Owens keeps it for boxer shorts.

  • brācae interiōrēs

    also used · modern · Traupman 400

See also trousers, T-shirt, underwear.

SourcesLewis & Short: subligaculum · Lewis & Short: subligar · Lewis & Short: femorale · Mir: morning routine (transcription)

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. undershorts. John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 400.
